subject.title: config: use datetime suffix for config backup files instead of numeric rotation

question: Should timestamped config backups preserve or convert existing numbered `.bak.N` recovery points, or may the migration delete them when the suffix scheme changes?
rationale: Config backups are a recovery surface, and repository policy treats config migration and fallback behavior as compatibility-sensitive rather than an automation-only choice.

options.title: Preserve legacy recovery points
options.body: Require this PR or a replacement to keep existing `.bak.N` files through migration or convert them into the timestamped retention set without silently deleting useful backups.

options.title: Prune legacy numbered backups
options.body: Accept that first-run cleanup after the change may delete existing numbered backups in exchange for one clean timestamp-only scheme.

options.title: Keep the numeric ring
options.body: Reject the timestamped naming change for now and keep the numbered ring as the intended stable behavior.

recommendation.title: Preserve legacy recovery points
recommendation.body: Require this PR or a replacement to keep existing `.bak.N` files through migration or convert them into the timestamped retention set without silently deleting useful backups.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest recent routing signal across config backup, recovery, and test history for this migration-policy decision.
